parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Fig. 1.1 shows a horizontal beam clamped at one end with a block attached to the other end. {{figure:fig_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

The block is made to oscillate vertically.

The Young modulus $E$ of the material of the beam is given by $$E = \frac{kM}{T^2}$$ where $M$ is the mass of the block, $T$ is the period of the oscillations and $k$ is a constant.

A student determines the values and percentage uncertainties of $k$, $M$ and $T$. Table 1.1 lists the percentage uncertainties.

Table 1.1

| quantity | percentage uncertainty |
| $k$ | $\pm 2.1\%$ |
| $M$ | $\pm 0.6\%$ |
| $T$ | $\pm 1.5\%$ |

The student uses the values of $k$, $M$ and $T$ to calculate the value of $E$ as $8.245 \times 10^9$Pa.
parts.text: (i) Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the value of $E$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: (ii) Use your answer in (b)(i) to determine the value of $E$, with its absolute uncertainty, to an appropriate number of significant figures.
